one_liner: Intel's tensor compiler backend for oneDNN Graph API that fuses MLP/MHA subgraphs; beat oneDNN post-op fusion and TVM. Removed in oneDNN 3.8.
what_it_does: An optional backend of the oneDNN Graph API: a framework hands over a partitioned DNN subgraph (MLP, multi-head attention, conv residual blocks) and the backend compiles it into one fused, JIT-generated kernel instead of a chain of oneDNN primitives. It was not a separate API; users built oneDNN with -DONEDNN_BUILD_GRAPH=ON -DONEDNN_EXPERIMENTAL_GRAPH_COMPILER_BACKEND=ON and went through the normal Graph API. Code lived in src/graph/backend/graph_compiler of the oneDNN tree (Apache-2.0) up to v3.7.
how_it_is_fast: It lowers through two IRs: a Graph IR that keeps op semantics for graph-level passes (layout propagation, constant-weight preprocessing, FP32-to-Int8 conversion with quantization-parameter folding) and a C-like Tensor IR for code generation. Compute-heavy ops are expanded from expert-written templates around tuned microkernels instead of being searched by an auto-scheduler. Fine-grain fusion inserts neighbouring ops at anchor points inside the template loops, and coarse-grain fusion merges the parallel outer loops of several fused ops, with buffer reuse by liveness analysis.
when_to_use: Only if you are pinned to oneDNN 3.0-3.7 on Intel Xeon and run Int8 or FP32 BERT-style MHA blocks through the Graph API (the paper reports 2.3-2.4x lower MHA time than post-op fusion).
As a reference design for template-plus-fusion tensor compilers, if you are building your own fused MLP/attention codegen for CPUs.
Reproducing the paper's BERT-Large / DLRM numbers on a Xeon Platinum 8358-class machine with a matching oneDNN 3.x build.
when_not_to_use: New projects: oneDNN 3.7 deprecated the backend and 3.8 removed it; current oneDNN covers SDPA and gated MLP through its regular Graph API backend.
FP32 MLP: the paper measured it 4% slower than plain oneDNN primitives.
Non-Intel or non-x86 targets: the paper only measured a Xeon Platinum 8358 and the docs list no other supported platforms.
Builds with the DPC++/SYCL CPU runtime: its CMake fails with an unsupported CPU runtime error for DPCPP.
Anything that needs stability: the backend was always labelled experimental.

integration.dependencies: part of oneDNN (static or shared per DNNL_LIBRARY_TYPE); optional LLVM >= 10 if the llvm JIT is selected, otherwise the builtin JIT needs nothing extra
integration.min_toolchain: not documented beyond oneDNN 3.x's own requirements
integration.platforms: x86-64 Intel Xeon as measured; other platforms not documented; OMP/TBB CPU runtimes only (DPCPP rejected)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same oneDNN Graph API, chosen at build time; frameworks needed no code change, but only oneDNN <= 3.7 ships it

gotchas: Off by default; it had to be enabled at CMake time, and runtime env vars ONEDNN_EXPERIMENTAL_GRAPH_COMPILER_CPU_JIT (llvm/c/builtin) and _OPT_LEVEL change codegen.
Removed in oneDNN v3.8, so upgrading oneDNN silently drops back to the regular dnnl backend's fusions.
The 'c' JIT mode is unavailable on Windows and macOS per its CMake file.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: LIBXSMM and Optimizing-DGEMM are kernel libraries you call directly, while this was a graph-level fuser behind the oneDNN Graph API; pick it only for whole-subgraph MHA/MLP fusion on an old oneDNN, since it is no longer maintained.
verified_claims_summary: Intel's own arXiv paper (2301.01333) measured on a 32-core Xeon Platinum 8358: BERT-Large 1.12x and DLRM 1.15x end to end over oneDNN post-op fusion, MHA 2.3x (FP32) / 2.4x (Int8) lower time than post-op fusion, and 2.4x (MLP) / 6.2x (MHA) average over TVM with auto-scheduler; FP32 MLP was 4% slower than oneDNN primitives and Int8 MLP 6% faster. No compiler, flags or benchmark scripts are given.
status_note: Discontinued: deprecated in oneDNN 3.7 and removed in 3.8 (2025); the code remains readable at the v3.7 tag under Apache-2.0, but it is a reference, not something to adopt.
